messages.subject: How to edit the legend
parts:
Hi

For a R and ggplot newbie I have a lot of difficulties to find any
useful information on how to edit the legend in a ggplot graph
straightforwardly, e.g. how to change the title or omit the legend
title at all, how to remove the frames ggplot puts around each symbol
in the legen, etc. Is there a useful help that would summarise those
steps?

Cheers
Martin

messages.author: 5ec5102a43e29af7
messages.subject: Re: How to edit the legend
parts:
On Sun, Feb 07, 2010 at 10:17:32PM -0800, waschbaer wrote:
> For a R and ggplot newbie I have a lot of difficulties to find any
> useful information on how to edit the legend in a ggplot graph
> straightforwardly, e.g. how to change the title or omit the legend
> title at all,

modifications like this one are done using the scale_* functions (see
[1]), the same family of functions that is used to modify the axes or
symbol size and others settings.

for example:

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(mtcars,aes(mpg,disp,colour=hp))+geom_point()

in this case, colour is scaled continuously, so to modify the colour
legend the function 'scale_colour_continuous()' is used (see
?scale_colour_continuous).

last_plot() + scale_colour_continuous("")

removes the legend title. With the parameters breaks, values, labels you
can define your own colour scale.

> how to remove the frames ggplot puts around each symbol
> in the legen, etc. Is there a useful help that would summarise those
> steps?

should be possible over the theme setting, the default is 'theme_gray()',
other themes for example 'theme_bw()' exists too and you can also define your own
themes. The default theme can be changed by 'theme_set(theme_bw())'.

Simply type the command 'theme_gray()' to have a look at the settings.

there is a key called 'legend.key' which defines the symbol background.

try:

last_plot() + opts(legend.key=theme_rect(fill="blue",colour="white"))

or

last_plot() + opts(legend.key=theme_rect(fill=NULL,colour="white"))


hope this helps.

regards,
stefan

[1] http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/
